title: Lazarus, the rich man, and bodies after death
english: One may raise a difficulty about Lazarus and the rich man. The simpler readers take the story as if both men, still with their bodies, receive what their lives deserved. More careful readers deny that the scene belongs to the resurrection: after the rising, no one is left still living in this age.

The rich man says, "[[I have five brothers; send Lazarus to tell them what is here, so they do not come into this place of torment >> Bible:Luke 16:28]]." From that speech people hunt for tongue, finger, Abraham's bosom, and the reclining place.

title: Soul-form like the earthly body; Samuel visible
english: …and earthly body can be taken that way. Whenever someone among those who have fallen asleep is reported as appearing, he is seen in a form like the one he had while he still wore flesh.

title: Before the resurrection the soul still uses a body
english: …poor man resting in Abraham's bosom—spoken of before the Savior's coming, before the world's consummation, and so before the resurrection—the one punished in Hades, the other at rest in Abraham's bosom—teach that even now, at departure, the soul uses a body.
From Methodius. Origen, having put it this way…

title: Those of the resurrection will be as angels—without flesh
english: …to declare the Lord, as when the Sadducees tempt him: "[[those who attain the resurrection will then be as angels >> Bible:Luke 20:36]]." He adds: "Angels stand outside flesh in the height of blessedness, and for that reason they also have glory; so we who are to be made equal to angels must likewise be bare of flesh as they are."
